one_line: One of Queen Jayadevi’s powerful brothers, a regent controlling Kashmir’s coinage and trade in the last decades of the Karkota dynasty.

appearance.face: oval face with sharp cheekbones, medium wheatish complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, intense narrow eyes with dark circles from long councils, default expression calm but calculating with a faint, knowing half-smile
appearance.hair: straight, dark brown-black hair pulled back into a low, tight knot at the nape; a simple narrow gold circlet with a tiny central turquoise cabochon resting above the forehead; sideburns short and tidy
appearance.costume: era-accurate Kashmiri royal-elite attire: a long-sleeved knee-length tunic (anga) in rich deep indigo wool with subtle woven geometric borders in muted gold along the neckline, cuffs and hem; over it a soft, finely woven pale saffron woollen shawl (uttariya) draped from the left shoulder across the torso and wrapped once around the forearms; fitted off-white cotton trousers (churidar-style, slightly ruched at the ankles) tucked into mid-calf soft leather boots dyed dark brown; a narrow dark red waist sash (patka) cinched at the midriff with a small engraved bronze clasp; jewellery limited to a short gold necklace with a single flat disc pendant and a pair of small gold hoop earrings, suggesting court status but not extreme extravagance
appearance.signature: a small leather coin-pouch tied to his sash, half-open to reveal a mix of neat silver Karkota coins and slightly duller, debased types, plus a single rolled palm-leaf document seal, symbolising his control over taxation, coinage and trade during the dynasty’s troubled decline as described by Kalhana

ref_desc: Mid-30s Kashmiri regent with oval wheatish face, low-knot dark hair and gold circlet, in deep indigo tunic, pale saffron shawl, off-white trousers, dark red sash, dark brown boots, carrying a mixed coin-pouch and palm-leaf seal in a gold-accented palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body shonen-anime style Kashmiri regent from c. 8th–9th century: a mid-30s man with an oval wheatish face, sharp cheekbones, short beard and moustache, intense narrow eyes and dark circles, his straight dark brown-black hair pulled into a low knot at the nape and topped with a narrow gold circlet bearing a tiny turquoise stone. He wears a long-sleeved knee-length deep indigo wool tunic with subtle muted-gold geometric borders at neckline, cuffs and hem, over fitted off-white cotton trousers slightly ruched at the ankles and tucked into mid-calf dark brown leather boots. A pale saffron wool shawl is draped from his left shoulder across the chest and wrapped once around the forearms, and a narrow dark red waist sash with a small bronze clasp cinches the tunic. Keep jewellery modest: a short gold necklace with a flat disc pendant and small gold hoop earrings. At his waist, clearly show his signature prop, a small leather coin-pouch tied to the sash, half-open to reveal brighter silver Karkota coins and duller debased coins, alongside a rolled palm-leaf document seal, symbolising his grip on coinage, taxation and trade; pose him standing in a neutral, dignified stance so all facial features, hairstyle, garments, boots and the coin-pouch are clearly visible, using a palette of deep indigo, pale saffron, dark red, off-white, dark brown and gold.
